h1: Bormio ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Bormio sits at 1,225 metres where three valleys meet, and the mountain above it does something few Alpine resorts can: one uninterrupted run of 8.5 kilometres from Cima Bianca at 3,017 metres down to the town, dropping 1,817 vertical metres - the greatest skiable vertical in Italy by the operator's own account. The Stelvio, the World Cup downhill, starts at 2,255 metres on the same slope.
stayOverview: The old town sits below the cable car with its thermal baths and medieval lanes; the newer quarter spreads towards the valley mouth and the road to Livigno.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. The old town puts you by the baths and within walking distance of the cable car.
rentalCars: Bormio is at the foot of the Stelvio pass, about two hours from Milan up the Valtellina.

baseElevation.unannounced: The operator states the lifts reach over 3,000 m and gives 1,817 m of vertical from Cima Bianca, and its ski map counts runs and lifts, but no page states the altitude the ski area starts at.

longestRun.note: The summit-to-base run from Cima Bianca at 3,017 m, with 1,817 m of vertical, down the crest to Cimino, through Conca Valbella, the S. Ambrogio and Praimont slopes, the Carcentina diagonal on the Stelvio and the Bosco Basso, ending at the cable car in town.

dayPass.note: The promo rate for a one-day Bormio-only pass from 4 to 18 December 2026; the operator publishes separate low and high-season lists, and buying online in advance saves up to 25%. A junior day is EUR 20.00.

facts.text: An uninterrupted 8.5 km run from Cima Bianca at 3,017 m to the valley, dropping 1,817 metres - the greatest skiable vertical in Italy by the operator’s own account.
The Stelvio, the World Cup downhill, starts at 2,255 m.
Three beginner areas, a kids area called Playwood and a funslope, alongside 10 blue runs.
The Jungle at 2,055 m splits into a beginner line of four small tables and an intermediate line of 5-6 metre jumps.
